transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been dealing with an intense, overwhelming fear of enclosed spaces and elevators. It has been going on for about 11 months now, and I finally decided I need some help with it.

When you’re in or thinking about enclosed spaces or elevators, do you ever have sudden panic attacks with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might lose control? Do these attacks ever happen out of the blue when you’re not in those situations?

Yes, my heart races and I get really short of breath whenever I'm in an elevator or even just thinking about being in one. However, they never happen out of the blue; I only feel that intense panic when it is directly related to those tight spaces.
Do you go out of your way to avoid elevators or other enclosed spaces, and has this fear been interfering with your work, daily activities, or relationships?

Yes, I completely avoid them and will walk up ten flights of stairs just to bypass an elevator. This has really started to impact my work because I've had to decline meetings on upper floors, which is incredibly frustrating and embarrassing.
Did this fear start after a specific frightening event in an elevator or enclosed space, such as getting trapped or feeling in danger?
No, I don't recall any specific frightening event, like getting trapped, that started all of this. The fear just seemed to develop on its own without a clear trigger.
Has this fear and avoidance been present most of the time for at least 6 months?
Yes, it definitely has. I've been dealing with this intense fear and avoiding elevators for about 11 months now. It has been a constant struggle for me almost every single day during that time.
